fit: methanolic celery seed extract and behavioral outcomes in alcohol-exposed mice
assessment: Groups have contradictory dose labels in the protocol and Results. Locomotion, stereotypy and social measures supply no visual hallucination counts. Seed preparation and model do not match the culinary Parkinson claim.

fit: regulatory adverse-event table for a commercial ethanolic seed extract
assessment: The assessment names hypotension in a 2,245-patient uncontrolled seed-extract series without event counts or orthostatic context. The 2000 author abstract likely overlaps and does not enumerate adverse event types. No cold-pressed oil or Parkinson comparison.

fit: branded pumpkin seed oil capsule and measured seated pressure versus placebo
assessment: Seated systolic change was −1.2 versus +1.0 mmHg (p = 0.496); diastolic change was −0.1 versus −0.8 (p = 0.813). No pressure after standing or scale for triggered lightheadedness. The complete capsule formula and pressing grade are unverified.

fit: dried celery stem-and-leaf powder versus starch and nonspecific safety monitoring
assessment: Fifty randomized, 36 analyzed in a cardiometabolic trial of dried stem-and-leaf powder at 750 mg/day. Weekly calls included possible side effects, and the report states none attributable to celery powder. No hallucination scale, Parkinson cohort or separately administered leaf. General safety reporting does not resolve symptom direction.
